Extremely Disappointing and Unethical Admission Process

We recently relocated from Delhi to Mumbai and inquired about admission at JBCN Parel. Most schools clearly informed us if seats were unavailable at the time of inquiry. However, JBCN’s admission team asked us to purchase an admission kit for ₹5,000 just to apply. Since I have two children, I initially enquired only for my elder one, planning to consider the younger one later. As soon as they found out about my younger child, they insisted that I purchase another ₹5,000 admission kit, claiming it would increase the elder one's chances due to the sibling factor.

They then called us to Mumbai for an interaction. Despite my poor health, I attended the session for my elder child, only to be told that there were no seats and we were placed on a waiting list. Shockingly, they called us back the next day for my younger child’s interaction—only to repeat the same thing: no seats available!

This entire process cost us ₹10,000 for admission kits, flight tickets, and 10 days of hotel expenses—completely wasted on false hopes. They misled us emotionally, mentally, and financially. If there are no seats in a particular branch, the school should not push parents to buy admission kits or schedule interactions.

In contrast, Aditya Birla and Edubridge International School were professional and transparent. They informed us upfront that they didn’t have seats. Edubridge even followed up with us when a seat became available and scheduled a school tour accordingly. This is called professionalism.

To make matters worse, JBCN had the audacity to suggest admission at their Chembur branch, expecting a young child to travel from Lower Parel to Chembur daily—without even providing a bus service!

JBCN, please do better. Admissions should be about a child's education, not just a business model to make money. Stop misleading parents and wasting their time and resources.

featured_reviews.name: Rhea Gursahani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Both my kids, Krrish and Koel have been with Da Vinci Montessori since Dec 2021 and we intend on continuing with the school as long as we are in the city and respective grades are supported by DVM.

Having experienced both the international and Montessori curriculums, I have seen my kids blossom into independent and opinionated individuals who also empathize and understand the situation around them, with the Montessori curriculum.

Koel was 14 months when she joined Da Vinci in the Toddler Class. 3 months ago, some of the students in Koel's class moved onto the Primary section. This also meant that several young kids now came to her class, and my little girl who once was a baby of the class transformed into the big sister. One day, as I was waiting to receive her, I was narrated a very sweet story by her teacher which touched my heart to the deepest levels.

As was informed, when the younger kids wanted something in class, Koel was the first one to notice, and she would stop whatever activity she was doing, to help the young child. One day, a young toddler was thirsty and made a gesture for the same. Koel noticed this from the other end of the class and ran to pour a glass of water for him. After sometime the young tod was thirsty again but instead of figuring what to do, he immediately went to look for Koel and asked her to pour him another glass of water.

Why I chose to share this story is because it very  beautifully depicts the empathy of the elder child and the independence of the younger one which all blossomed with their simple interaction in class. While the curriculum covers the knowledge aspect, it is these interactions of a mixed age classroom that really transform these young children into independent and caring humans.

Being the 2nd child and a COVID era baby, Koel did not enjoy as much Mama playtime and attention that her elder brother did, but, whatever she has learnt be it life skills, motor skills, empathy, language, knowledge has all been from DVM.

When Krrish joined DVM, he was 4.5 years old and we were returning from a post COVID era. If COVID was tough on us, it was worse with the kids who lost their sense of social being. Krrish was always pro learning but online schooling really got him disinterested in the concept of school. However, with the independence of choice given in the Montessori classroom, Krrish's love for school and learning was back. He was able to pick up the concepts quickly and now is a part of the Elementary class.

So while DVM is a beautiful option for Montessori what sets them apart are the people behind it and the genuine care and affection for the children and their well being. While the ideology is traditional the outlook is modern, to enable children to be successful in the fact paced, tech controlled life today!

Even while being a Montessori curriculum, the children are exposed to a variety of activities on par with international schools, such as Art, Speech and Drama, Physical Fitness, Capoeira, Spanish Music, in the Elementary classroom, and Music, Art, Fitness and Yoga in the Primary and Toddler classrooms.

The head of the school, Ms. Ashani, is deeply invested in ensuring that while the kids continue to learn from the Montessori classroom their future is safeguarded too, hence working on several tie ups with prominent big schools and introducing kids to a variety of inter school activities. The sincerity runs top down and the love, concern and nurturing can be seen in all members of the school from the administrator to each of the teachers in the Toddler, Primary and Elemnentary classroom, as well as the Didis!

I couldn't have asked for a better school for my kids! Thank you for making us a part of the DVM family!

According to us, in playgroup and nursery, the best thing to be done is to inculcate curiosity and interest for future studies. Teachers at Learning Steps did exactly this! Our kid was never overburdened. Textbooks are there. Homeworks are given. However its not the usual competitive race. Teachers are very sensible and understand that every child is different. Children are not forced to perform. The impact was clearly visible in our son. He used to be very excited to go to school. Even on Sundays he used to ask whether there is school! We feel this is ample evidence for the comfortable, accomodative and student friendly environment in Learning Steps. Detailed assessment of the child's performance is given at the end of every term in nursery in the form of a progress report. Batch size ranged between 10-15. The individual attention that our son has received has helped him phenomenally. We will always be indebted to the teaching and non-teaching staff at Learning Steps for the quality improvement they brought about in our son's life.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Thank you so much for your positive feedback 🙏🏻 Feedback like yours is valuable to us. It helps us continue to improve and provide the best possible experience for the kids. Thank you, and have a great day!

featured_reviews.name: Ganesh Moota
featured_reviews.review_text:
For anyone preparing for competitive exams like JEE Mains, JEE Advanced or MH-CET then the factors to consider are -
1. Bifocal - vocational subject ( instead of studying 2 different subjects)
2. Integrated college - ( both college and tution lectures will be scheduled in the same classrooms)
3. Quality of Study material provided
4. Infrastructure of Labs and Maintenance
5. Supportive staff (provided you are genuine hardworking student)
6. A class filled with students providing tough competition ( you won't like it if you want to chill and hangout by bunking classes).

And most importantly listen to reviews of those students who have studied from this college and have actually secured good grades ( don't make a perception on someone's review, it's their perception and his/her feedback depends on their actions and behaviour which is subjective).

Is this review reliable then?
You can say Yes, because I have studied from this college in batch 2015-2017 and have secured 90.77% in HSC and 158/200 in MH-CET, you can verify it on their academic calendar of distinction students for year 2017 🙂

Will also like to mention here that I had studied for 2 years here for FREE, because I was from BMC school prior to this.
